## Optional layers and interpretation

The compact schema 1.0.0 keeps DIA-NN matrices in core. Full report quantities require `proteovault add-layer DATABASE --layer quant-details`. This reader supports the compact layout only.

Protein sequences can be added to an existing vault with
`proteovault add-fasta DATABASE --fasta SEARCH_DATABASE.fasta`. The imported
reference appears as the `fasta` layer in `vault_info()`.

Published QC metrics require `proteovault add-layer DATABASE --layer qc` when the QC pipeline finished after the vault was built. Use `tbl_qc_metrics(vault)` to query them.

Default PSM access selects FDR-filtered validation observations. Search-stage PSMs require `proteovault add-layer DATABASE --layer raw-search`; PIN access requires `--layer msbooster`. Close and reopen an R handle after adding a layer.

Protein inference groups and quantitative DIA-NN groups remain separate. Group IDs are local to a database, group types remain distinct, and group quantities are not replicated to each member protein. No additional FDR filtering, normalization, log transformation, imputation, or sample renaming occurs.

The current schema stores precursor quantities, not summarized peptide quantities. Do not interpret different charges or modifications as independent summarized peptides. Plot functions return objects; figure export remains under the caller's control.

`summarize_quantification_coverage()` reports how many samples quantify each feature, including features with zero positive samples. Its `n_samples` and `total_samples` columns distinguish the cohort union from the across-sample intersection.
